definition: The Parents & Kids Safe AI Coalition is a political action committee that advocates for regulation of artificial intelligence on child safety.
details: As of April 2026, the group is funded solely by the artificial intelligence company OpenAI, which pledged $10 million to the effort.

explainer.lead: The Parents & Kids Safe AI Coalition is a political action committee advocating regulation of AI on child safety. As of April 2026 it is funded solely by OpenAI, which pledged $10 million to the effort.

tiers.eli5: It is a campaign group that pushes for rules to keep AI safe for children, and an AI company pays for it.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners track the coalition as a regulatory signal when building products aimed at minors. The pitfall is reading its positions as neutral; its single disclosed funder shapes how its advocacy is perceived.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a political action committee, a US campaign-finance entity, not a technical method, so no definition or formula applies. Its documented limit is disclosure: as of April 2026 the sole funder named is OpenAI, with a $10 million pledge.

explainer.example: A team designing a child-facing chatbot cites the coalition's advocacy when deciding to add stricter safety filters.
